title: Software license and support
purpose: Twelve-page synthetic software agreement with distinct operational clauses, distant references and an explicit final-page payment override. Length and extraction are testable; no legal-risk gold label is prescribed.

sections.heading: 1.1. Purpose and defined service
sections.text: Example Supplier provides a fictional inventory application to Example Customer for internal business use. The application receives product descriptions, records inventory movements and produces downloadable summaries. The service includes access to the hosted application, standard documentation and the support described in this agreement. It excludes payment processing, identity verification and any decision about whether a product may lawfully be sold. A reference to the application includes ordinary updates supplied during the subscription. A reference to customer material means information uploaded or entered by Example Customer, excluding technical measurements generated by the service.

sections.heading: 1.2. Contract documents
sections.text: This agreement consists of these numbered clauses and the Order Schedule on page 12. The schedule identifies the subscription period, licensed locations and initial charges. Operational messages, product announcements and descriptions displayed inside the application do not amend either document. A change must identify the affected clause and state the replacement wording in a written record accepted by both parties. If a schedule expressly identifies a clause that it overrides, the identified override controls that subject only. Other provisions continue to apply without an implied amendment.

sections.heading: 1.3. Administration and interpretation
sections.text: Each party will appoint a business contact through its own internal process, without including contact details in this document. A business day means a day on which both parties ordinarily conduct business, excluding agreed closure days. Periods stated only as days are calendar days. Headings assist navigation and do not expand an obligation. Neither party may infer exclusivity from this arrangement. Example Customer remains responsible for deciding whether the documented functions meet its needs before placing operational reliance on the service or replacing an existing system.

sections.heading: 2.1. Granted access
sections.text: During a paid subscription, Example Supplier grants Example Customer a limited right to access the application for the licensed locations. Staff and temporary contractors may use the service while acting for Example Customer and following its instructions. The license does not permit a separate business to operate its own inventory through the subscription. Example Customer may retain exported summaries after access ends, subject to the confidentiality provisions. Downloaded documentation may be copied internally for training, provided notices identifying its source remain intact and the copies are not offered as a competing product.

sections.heading: 2.2. Limits and responsibility
sections.text: Example Customer must not resell access, publish access credentials, bypass documented technical restrictions or use the application to distribute harmful files. Automated access is permitted only through the documented import and export interfaces. Testing that could degrade availability requires a separately agreed plan defining timing, traffic limits and recovery arrangements. Example Customer is responsible for instructions issued by its authorized personnel, but is not responsible for activity attributable to an access-control failure caused by Example Supplier. Neither party may treat ordinary data export as an attempt to reproduce the application.

sections.heading: 2.3. Capacity review
sections.text: The subscription includes the capacity recorded in the schedule rather than an unlimited processing entitlement. When measured use regularly exceeds that capacity, Example Supplier will provide a written summary explaining the measurement and proposed adjustment. No additional charge applies retrospectively without agreement. The parties will first consider reducing unnecessary background imports or changing the processing window. If they cannot agree a revised allowance, Example Customer may continue within the existing allowance for the remaining subscription. A temporary burst does not by itself authorize suspension or automatic purchase of a higher service level.

pages.heading: 3. Delivery and acceptance

sections.heading: 3.1. Initial preparation
sections.text: Example Supplier will make a trial workspace available before the subscription start date. Example Customer will provide a small fictional import file and identify the supported browser versions it intends to use. The initial configuration includes one inventory template, standard export settings and a demonstration import. Custom integrations, historical data correction and replacement hardware are outside this preparation work. Each party will record any missing dependency that prevents testing, together with the action needed to resolve it. A dependency delay shifts the affected preparation date only, unless the parties agree a wider change.

sections.heading: 3.2. Acceptance procedure
sections.text: Example Customer has ten business days after delivery to compare the configured workspace with the documented acceptance examples. A rejection notice must describe a reproducible material mismatch and include enough information to distinguish it from an unsupported request. Example Supplier will correct the mismatch and resubmit the affected example. The test period restarts for that example, not for functions already accepted. Use solely for testing is not acceptance. Operational use of an unaffected function does not waive a previously notified failure in another function. Silence at the end of the test period requires a reminder before deemed acceptance.

sections.heading: 3.3. Outstanding items
sections.text: The parties may accept the service subject to a written list of minor outstanding items and target correction dates. That list must say whether a temporary workaround is available and who will verify completion. An accepted limitation cannot later be presented as a newly discovered defect unless its actual effect differs materially from the recorded description. Clause 10.1 on page 10 governs the continuing performance warranty after acceptance. Acceptance does not transfer ownership of customer material, remove the export obligation or convert a separately priced enhancement into included maintenance.

text_anchors: Use solely for testing is not acceptance

sections.heading: 4.1. Charges and ordinary deadline
sections.text: Subscription and preparation charges are listed in the schedule and are expressed in GBP. Unless an express schedule override applies, invoices are payable within 30 days of receipt. The invoice must identify the relevant subscription period and distinguish recurring charges from accepted additional work. Charges for work not requested by Example Customer are not payable merely because that work was performed. Clause S2 on page 12 sets a different deadline for the initial order and expressly overrides this ordinary deadline. This deliberate difference tests whether a reviewer reads the schedule together with the main terms.

sections.heading: 4.2. Disputed amounts
sections.text: Example Customer may dispute an invoice by describing the challenged amount and the reason for the challenge before the applicable payment deadline. Undisputed amounts remain payable on time. The parties will compare the invoice with the accepted order, service period and any approved changes. Example Supplier will issue a corrected invoice when the comparison confirms an error. A disputed amount does not become overdue while that comparison is being conducted in good faith. Neither party is required to disclose unrelated commercial records when a narrower record is sufficient to explain the calculation.

sections.heading: 4.3. Adjustments and purchasing controls
sections.text: Recurring prices remain fixed for the initial subscription. A proposed renewal increase must be communicated with the renewal notice and cannot take effect during the current period. Example Customer's internal purchasing reference may appear on an invoice for administration, but its absence does not change a correctly agreed charge. Additional work requires a written estimate identifying scope, charging basis and a maximum authorized amount. When the maximum would be exceeded, Example Supplier must pause that additional work and obtain approval. No automatic currency conversion, late fee or minimum purchase is created by this clause.

sections.heading: 5.1. Support requests
sections.text: Example Supplier provides support during a shared eight-hour business-day window agreed at onboarding. A request should state the affected function, approximate time of the event, steps already attempted and whether a workaround is available. Example Customer should use invented records when reproducing an issue whenever those records demonstrate the same behavior. Example Supplier may request a limited diagnostic extract only when necessary to investigate. Support does not include entering inventory on Example Customer's behalf, reconciling inaccurate source records or teaching general computer skills unrelated to the application.

sections.heading: 5.2. Response priorities
sections.text: A critical incident prevents all ordinary access without an available workaround. A major incident materially impairs an important function but leaves some operations possible. A routine request concerns a minor defect, explanation or improvement suggestion. Example Supplier will acknowledge critical incidents within four support hours and major incidents within one business day. These are acknowledgment targets, not promises that every underlying defect can be corrected within the same period. The parties may reclassify a request when evidence changes, but a reclassification must state the operational reason rather than merely restart the response clock.

sections.heading: 5.3. Release management
sections.text: Routine updates should preserve documented import formats and ordinary export readability. Example Supplier will announce a material interface change at least twenty days before removing the previous interface. An urgent security correction may be applied sooner, with a description of its operational effect as soon as practicable. Example Customer is not required to purchase an optional module to retain an existing contracted function during the subscription. Deprecated functions must remain usable until their stated withdrawal date. Maintenance records will identify the release affected by a defect so that repeated reports can be distinguished from unrelated incidents.

pages.heading: 6. Availability and continuity

sections.heading: 6.1. Availability measurement
sections.text: The monthly availability target is 99.5 percent, measured at the application's ordinary access boundary. An unavailable minute occurs when a valid request cannot reach the principal inventory functions because of a service fault. Example Customer's device failure, its local network outage and a refusal caused by an invalid request are excluded. Planned maintenance is excluded only when announced at least three business days beforehand and kept within the announced two-hour window. Time beyond that window counts as unavailable. Measurements must retain enough detail to explain the calculation without retaining the content of inventory records.

sections.heading: 6.2. Credits and repeated failures
sections.text: If the target is missed, Example Customer may request a credit equal to five percent of the monthly subscription charge for the affected month. A request must identify the month and be made within forty-five days after it ends. The credit is applied to a later invoice or refunded if no later invoice is due. Credits are not an exclusive remedy for every kind of service failure. Clause 11.2 on page 11 provides a separate ending right when repeated availability failures satisfy its stated threshold. A support acknowledgment alone does not prove that availability was restored.

sections.heading: 6.3. Continuity measures
sections.text: Example Supplier will maintain an operational recovery procedure covering service configuration, recent customer material and access to essential dependencies. Recovery exercises will use synthetic records where practical and record the observed restoration time. Example Customer should retain periodic exports suitable for its own continuity needs; doing so does not excuse Example Supplier from its backup obligations. The parties will distinguish restoration of access from reconciliation of changes entered near an interruption. A recovered environment must not silently replace newer customer records with older copies without identifying the affected period and available reconciliation choices.

text_anchors: five percent of the monthly subscription charge

pages.heading: 7. Customer material and handling

sections.heading: 7.1. Control and permitted processing
sections.text: Example Customer retains control of customer material and grants Example Supplier only the rights needed to host, transmit, back up and support the contracted service. Example Supplier must not sell that material, use it to advertise to unrelated businesses or include it in a general training dataset. Aggregated operational measurements may be used to improve reliability only when they do not reveal individual inventory descriptions or allow customer material to be reconstructed. An improvement project requiring identifiable customer content needs a separate written agreement describing its purpose, duration and deletion arrangements.

sections.heading: 7.2. Imports and correction
sections.text: Example Customer is responsible for selecting what it imports and for confirming that it is entitled to provide those records. The service is intended for fictional product and stock information, not sensitive personal records. Import validation will identify unsupported columns and malformed quantities before applying a batch where practicable. A rejected row must remain distinguishable from a successfully applied row. Example Supplier will provide a documented method to correct or remove erroneous imports without requiring Example Customer to disclose unrelated source files. The parties will preserve an appropriate record of a correction without retaining the removed content indefinitely.

sections.heading: 7.3. Export and deletion
sections.text: Standard exports must include current product records and the transaction history included in the subscription, in a documented machine-readable format. Example Customer may request an export during the subscription without stating an intention to leave. Clause 11.3 on page 11 describes the final export window after the service ends. After that window, Example Supplier will delete active copies within thirty days unless the parties agree a narrower retained dataset for a stated purpose. Backup copies may expire through the ordinary rotation, must remain access-restricted and must not be restored to ordinary service merely to extend retention.

text_anchors: delete active copies within thirty days

pages.heading: 8. Security and confidentiality

sections.heading: 8.1. Protective measures
sections.text: Example Supplier will restrict administrative access to personnel who need it for an assigned service task. Access permissions must be reviewed when duties change and removed when no longer required. Transfers of customer material across public networks will use encrypted connections, and stored backups will have access controls separate from ordinary application access. Example Customer will protect its own access methods and promptly report a suspected compromise. Neither party is required to reveal working credentials to demonstrate compliance. Security questionnaires should be answered through control descriptions or suitable independent evidence rather than unrestricted access to operational systems.

sections.heading: 8.2. Incident coordination
sections.text: A security incident means confirmed unauthorized access to customer material or a confirmed loss of its integrity within the service. Example Supplier will notify Example Customer without undue delay after confirming such an incident and provide the information then reasonably available. An initial notice may distinguish confirmed facts from matters still being investigated. Updates will describe affected functions, containment steps and recommended customer actions. The parties will coordinate preservation of relevant evidence while avoiding unnecessary copies of the affected material. A routine blocked attempt is not automatically an incident requiring individual notice under this clause.

sections.heading: 8.3. Confidential information
sections.text: Each party will protect non-public business, technical and pricing information received from the other with reasonable care and use it only for this relationship. Information already public, independently developed or lawfully obtained without restriction is excluded. Necessary disclosure to advisers or service personnel is permitted only under equivalent confidentiality duties. If a disclosure requirement applies, the receiving party will limit the disclosure and provide advance notice where permitted. These duties continue for three years after the subscription ends. Customer material remains subject to the more specific processing and deletion obligations rather than becoming unrestricted when that period expires.

text_anchors: three years after the subscription ends

pages.heading: 9. Intellectual property and claims

sections.heading: 9.1. Existing materials
sections.text: Example Supplier retains its pre-existing application code, general documentation and reusable methods. Example Customer retains its pre-existing templates, product descriptions and other material supplied for the service. A configuration that combines these materials does not transfer ownership of either underlying contribution. The subscription price includes the access rights expressly granted here, not an assignment of source code. If the parties commission a separately owned deliverable, the corresponding order must identify that deliverable and state the intended ownership rule. Neither party may remove the other's ownership notices from material it is permitted to copy.

sections.heading: 9.2. Feedback and improvements
sections.text: Example Customer may suggest improvements without being required to supply them. Example Supplier may implement a general suggestion without owing a separate fee, provided it does not disclose confidential customer material or claim ownership of an independently supplied specification. A feedback message does not itself authorize publication of the message, use of a business name in marketing or access to additional records. Where an improvement depends on a custom workflow, the parties will clarify whether it becomes a supported standard function or a separately maintained extension before either relies on a delivery commitment.

sections.heading: 9.3. Third-party objections
sections.text: If a third party claims that authorized use of the application infringes its intellectual property, Example Customer will promptly provide the relevant notice and reasonable cooperation. Example Supplier may control the response but must not agree a settlement imposing an admission or unrelated obligation on Example Customer without consent. Example Supplier may obtain continued use rights, modify the affected function without materially reducing it, or replace it with a comparable function. If none is reasonably available, Example Customer may end the affected subscription and receive a refund for its unused prepaid period. Customer-supplied material is excluded from this supplier commitment.

text_anchors: not an assignment of source code

pages.heading: 10. Performance and responsibility

sections.heading: 10.1. Limited performance warranty
sections.text: During the subscription, Example Supplier will use reasonable skill and care and the application will materially conform to its agreed documentation. Example Customer must report a reproducible failure with information reasonably needed to investigate. Example Supplier will first correct the failure or provide a workable alternative that does not materially reduce the contracted function. If neither is supplied within thirty days after a complete report, Example Customer may end the affected function and recover unused prepaid charges attributable to it. This warranty does not promise uninterrupted operation or the accuracy of source information entered by Example Customer.

sections.heading: 10.2. Liability allocation
sections.text: Each party's aggregate liability arising from this agreement is limited to the subscription charges paid or payable for the preceding twelve months. The limit does not apply to unpaid agreed fees, deliberate misuse of the other party's confidential information or a payment expressly required by the intellectual-property claim procedure. Neither party accepts liability for losses that the other could reasonably have avoided using the documented export facilities after receiving a specific warning. A party relying on that exclusion must identify the warning and the practical avoidance step, rather than assuming that any backup would have prevented every loss.

sections.heading: 10.3. Review of a claim
sections.text: A party raising a claim will describe the event, the contractual obligation involved and the reasonably available evidence of its effect. Both parties will take proportionate steps to limit continuing disruption while preserving relevant records. A temporary workaround does not itself settle a disputed claim or waive a properly notified defect. Any agreed settlement must identify the matters it resolves and whether service obligations continue. These invented limits and remedies are provided as reviewable contract text; this fixture does not prescribe a legal conclusion about their enforceability, fairness or suitability for any actual transaction.

text_anchors: within thirty days after a complete report

sections.heading: 11.1. Subscription and renewal
sections.text: The initial subscription lasts twelve months from the date identified in the schedule. It renews for successive twelve-month periods unless either party gives notice at least thirty days before the current period ends. Example Supplier must send a renewal reminder at least sixty days before that date, identifying any proposed price change. If the reminder is late, Example Customer may decline renewal until fifteen days after receiving it, even if the ordinary notice deadline has passed. Continued testing in an export-only workspace after expiry does not create a new subscription.

sections.heading: 11.2. Ending the subscription
sections.text: Either party may end the subscription for a material breach that remains uncorrected thirty days after a written notice describing the breach and required correction. Example Customer may also end it after the availability target is missed in three consecutive months, provided notice is given within thirty days after the third month. This repeated-failure right operates separately from service credits. Suspension for overdue undisputed fees requires a further ten-day warning and must preserve access to the standard export function. A genuine invoice dispute does not authorize suspension of the entire service.

sections.heading: 11.3. Exit assistance and survival
sections.text: For twenty business days after the subscription ends, Example Supplier will provide export-only access to customer material without an additional subscription charge. Example Customer may request one explanation of the export structure during that window. Additional transformation or migration work requires a separate estimate and approval. The final export window must not be shortened by closing the ordinary interactive workspace. Accrued payment duties, confidentiality, ownership and the agreed responsibility provisions continue where their wording requires. After the export window, the deletion timetable in clause 7.3 applies, including its separate treatment of restricted backup copies.

sections.heading: S1. Order details and precedence
sections.text: This fictional order covers three licensed inventory locations and a combined allowance of forty thousand inventory movements per month. The initial subscription begins on 1 October 2026 and ends on 30 September 2027. The annual subscription charge is GBP 2400, invoiced at the start of the period, and the one-time preparation charge is GBP 300 after delivery of the configured trial workspace. No premium module or bespoke integration is ordered. Except for the express payment override below, these order details supplement the main clauses without replacing their remedies, export rights or renewal procedure.

sections.heading: S2. Express payment override
sections.text: For invoices issued under this initial order, payment is due within 14 days of receipt, not the ordinary thirty-day period. This sentence expressly overrides the payment deadline in clause 4.1 on page 4. It does not alter the treatment of disputed amounts in clause 4.2 or permit unapproved additional charges. The override applies to both the initial subscription invoice and the preparation invoice. A later renewal order uses the main agreement's ordinary deadline unless that later order expressly repeats or replaces this override. The earlier thirty-day wording is retained intentionally to test distant-clause reconciliation.

sections.heading: S3. Delivery assumptions and confirmation
sections.text: The initial import example will contain invented product descriptions and quantities only. Example Customer will nominate its three locations internally without adding addresses or individual names to this synthetic agreement. Preparation is expected to finish within fifteen business days after the example file is supplied in the documented format. The acceptance procedure in clause 3.2 remains unchanged. Neither party may interpret the estimated preparation date as a waiver of the acceptance examples. This schedule closes the complete twelve-page test document; it contains no signatures, actual account references or evidence of a real purchase.
